nominees.name: Hideo Hosono
nominees.affiliation: Tokyo Institute of Technology (Institute of Science Tokyo), Japan

motivation: In 2008 Kamihara, Hosono and co-workers reported superconductivity at 26 K in fluorine-doped LaFeAsO. This was the first new family of high-temperature superconductors since the cuprates. Within months, transition temperatures above 50 K were reached, and dozens of related iron pnictides and chalcogenides followed. The discovery overturned the long-held belief that magnetic iron is hostile to superconductivity. It also gave physicists a second, chemically distinct family in which to test ideas about unconventional pairing. The materials revealed new organising principles, including spin-fluctuation-mediated sign-changing pairing, electronic nematicity and quantum criticality, which have shaped condensed matter physics worldwide. They also offer promise for high-field wires. Hosono's broader record of oxide and mixed-anion materials design, including transparent amorphous oxide semiconductors, shows that deliberate materials discovery can open whole fields of physics.
